assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: @TableTest annotations present on lines 13, 28, 43, 67, 84 across five test methods

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing item operations, coupon logic, total calculation, and checkout.
assertions.evidence: Five separate methods: addItem, removeItem, couponApplication, checkout, calculateTotal each test distinct concern

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: 3 rows for add, 4 for remove, 6 for coupon (3 types + variants), 5 for checkout, 6 for total calc

assertions.text: Item operations (add/remove), coupon application (validity and replacement), cart total calculation (coupon type effects on price), and checkout (stock verification) are in separate @TableTest methods.
assertions.evidence: addItem, removeItem, couponApplicationResult, calculateTotal, checkout in separate methods

assertions.text: Each table row is independently executable — no row depends on a prior row's result. The table expresses rules, not a sequential test script. Each row specifies its own preconditions (e.g. 'Cart with items' as an input column, not implied from a previous row).
assertions.evidence: Each row has complete preconditions: 'Cart items before', 'Inventory', 'Coupon in store', 'Previous active code'

assertions.text: Coupon application table uses before/after columns (e.g. 'Active coupon' / 'Active coupon after?') to specify the state change when entering, replacing, or entering invalid coupon codes.
assertions.evidence: 'Previous active code' | 'Active code after?' columns in couponApplicationResult table

assertions.text: Coupon application table tests validity and replacement (valid code, expired code, nonexistent code, replacing active coupon) — not coupon type effects on price. Coupon type effects belong in the cart total table.
assertions.evidence: couponApplicationResult tests {valid, expired, nonexistent, replacement}; type effects in calculateTotal('Percentage off whole cart', 'Fixed amount off')

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: 'Scenario' appears as leftmost column in all five tables

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Message?', 'Total?', 'Active coupon after?')
assertions.evidence: 'Items after?', 'Stored price?', 'Message?' in addItem; 'Active code after?' in coupon; 'Total?' in calculateTotal

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Add to empty cart', 'Replace active coupon with expired') — not outcomes ('Error', 'Success').
assertions.evidence: 'Add to empty cart', 'Remove item not in cart', 'Expired coupon', 'Insufficient stock: widget-1' describe conditions not outcomes

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Product', 'Quantity', 'Message?', 'Cart total?') — not code identifiers like 'productId', 'result'.
assertions.evidence: 'Product ID', 'Qty', 'Catalogue', 'Cart items', 'Message?', 'Active coupon after?' use business terms

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: All five test methods contain only arrange-act-assert: buildCart/Catalogue, new ShoppingCartService().method(), assertAll()

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: couponApplicationResult and calculateTotal use @Description before @TableTest; no other annotations present

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 'Add Item Stores Catalogue Price...', 'Remove Item Updates Cart...', 'Coupon Application Result', 'Checkout Verifies Stock...', 'Calculate Total Applies Discount...'

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description in couponApplicationResult and calculateTotal both use triple-quoted text blocks ("""...""") not concatenation

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method has a single, uniform assertion pattern applied to all rows — not different assertions per scenario.
assertions.evidence: All methods use assertAll() with uniform assertions per method (e.g., assertEquals message + items, never varying per row)

assertions.text: Product prices and coupon rules (type, amount, expiry status) are visible in the table via columns, @Description, or explicit setup — not silently hardcoded. The reader can trace how inputs lead to outputs.
assertions.evidence: Catalogue [widget-1: 10.00], 'SAVE10=PERCENTAGE:0.10:valid', @Description explains coupon/discount behavior

assertions.text: TypeConverter methods are used to convert map/string table values into domain objects (e.g. Map → Cart, Map → InventoryService, map → Coupon). Test method bodies contain only arrange-act-assert — no object construction from raw table values.
assertions.evidence: parseCouponStore() and parseCoupon() TypeConverters; test bodies use buildCart(), buildCatalogue(), buildInventory() helpers only

assertions.text: Columns representing maps (e.g. cart contents, product catalogue, inventory levels) use standard TableTest map syntax — [k: v, k2: v2] for entries and [:] for empty map — not a custom bracket notation.
assertions.evidence: [widget-1: 2], [widget-1: 10.00, gadget-2: 15.00], [:] syntax used consistently across all map columns

assertions.text: Coupon data is expressed in a single column with a @TypeConverter — not spread across separate sparse columns for coupon type, value, and target product. The column format may be map syntax (e.g. [type: PERCENTAGE, value: 10]) or readable shorthand (e.g. '20% cart', '$5 off', '50% off widget').
assertions.evidence: 'Coupon in store' column with parseCouponStore() TypeConverter; 'Coupon' column with parseCoupon() TypeConverter; no separate type/value/product columns

assertions.text: @Description annotations do not repeat information that the scenario names already convey. Coupon type behavior (what PERCENTAGE/FIXED/PRODUCT mean) should be expressed through descriptive scenario names, not duplicated in the description.
assertions.evidence: couponApplicationResult @Description explains replacement/validity logic, defers type effects to calculateTotal; calculateTotal @Description explains product-specific/floor behavior, scenarios convey type labels
